extraction.Name: Charles Clifford, junior
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee to his 160 allotment at the time it was issued, as he did not want to pay taxes, but was told that it would be taxed any way, so he took it
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to William Charles, of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $350.00; in 1924, they foreclosed on his place
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: got behind in taxes, and, in 1920, he mortgaged to William Charles, of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $350.00, keeping up the payments for three years, paying $35.00, then he had hard luck, and, in 1924, they foreclosed on his place
extraction.Occupation/Income: farms on a rented place for his living
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, health pretty good; has a wife and five children to support, all of whom have good health; finds it pretty close living off of what he raises, especially when he gets hailed out — experienced this three years in succession; has never received any aid from the County, State or the United States Government; document subscribed November 24, 1928 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
